review_candidates.description: What We Can Achieve Together The Nature Conservancy (TNC ) is seeking a passionate and visionary leader to serve as the Gabon Sustainable Conservation Finance Director . The ideal candidate will demonstrate exceptional leadership and foster a collaborative, inclusive work environment where team members are empowered to contribute their unique talents and expertise. Reporting to the Gabon Country Director, the Director will oversee the integrated implementation of the Project Finance for Permanence (PFP) and Blue Bonds (BB) programs, ensuring that TNC provides robust technical, operational, and management support to the Government of Gabon. They will serve as the primary liaison to government agencies, conservation organizations, foundations, academic institutions, media, and TNC’s Global and Regional Leadership Teams. Key responsibilities include monitoring and reporting on project performance and risk, contributing to internal and external communications, developing and managing budgets and workplans, and supervising staff. The role involves high-level engagement with government partners, program management units, and the Conservation Trust Fund for Gabon (Fonds de Protection de la Biodiversité au Gabon – FPBG) , while coordinating technical expertise across TNC’s Gabon country team, Africa region, and global networks. Government Partnership and Public Sector Engagement :- Support partner ministries at both technical and political levels, working closely with program management units to strengthen capacity and ensure effective governance, negotiate and manage complex agreements with political sensitivity, build and maintain strategic partnerships with key stakeholders in the green-economy sectors and support eco-friendly policy development. Institutional Arrangements- Collaborate with FPBG and other institutions to establish robust financial, fiduciary, and operational structures that ensure long-term sustainability of conservation efforts. Strategic Leadership- Define and drive an integrated workplan for SFMs and improved communities’ sustainable livelihoods delivery, ensuring streamlined coordination, alignment of activities, and timely achievement of key deliverables. Internal Coordination- Serve as the central link between TNC’s Gabon country program and its Africa and global teams across sustainable finance mechanism and sustainable development goals (SDGs), support alignment with Congo Basin strategy, operate within a matrixed organization, collaborate with relevant colleagues across teams without direct supervisory authority. Fundraising & Donor Engagement- Partner with TNC’s country and Africa Development teams to prepare proposals, reports, and materials to mobilize resources for implementation. Project management: support the implementation and development of SFMs, strategic reflection on sustainable financial models for conservation, support the development and implementation of community-based sustainable activities and GCF related activities. Technical support: Provide technical support to government main partners especially for the implementation of all kinds of SFMs in all natural resources management sectors and tourism, support review and assessment of technical reports and strategies included related to community-based activities. Provide technical support for local talent capacity building programs Monitoring & Reporting- Oversee performance tracking, risk management, and reporting to the PFP Steering Committee, FPBG Board, Enduring Earth partnership, donors, and TNC leadership. Representation- Act as TNC’s focal point for Gabon’s SFM strategy initiatives and communities’ sustainable livelihoods with government, multilateral partners, donors, private sector stakeholders, and international platforms, Support communication strategies and prepare internal and external briefing materials Staff Development: Ensure the Gabon Teams staff are trained, supported, and mentored to achieve their highest potential. Compliance & Validation- Serve as TNC Gabon’s point of contact for the SFM development. Travel: Domestic and international travel as needed. Supervisory Responsibilities: Provide supervisory responsibilities as needed. This position reports to the Gabon Country Program Director. Proven track record in delivering large-scale, complex programs of strategic importance. Experience engaging with senior political and ministerial leadership, as well as technical ministries and institutions. Strong knowledge of biodiversity, conservation finance (including PFP and Blue Bonds), climate mitigation, or natural resource management. Demonstrated project management expertise, including oversight of multidisciplinary teams, timelines, and budgets. Experience negotiating complex agreements involving governments, donors, and multilateral institutions. Supervisory experience, with a demonstrated ability to lead teams and manage performance effectively. Strong problem-solving, facilitation, and conflict-resolution skills. Excellent written and spoken communication skills in both English and French (required). Desired Qualifications Master’s degree in conservation finance, international development, economics, public policy, environmental science, or a related field. Deep understanding of conservation and development contexts in Africa, particularly Central Africa. Experience working with Conservation Trust Funds or other long-term sustainable finance mechanisms. Prior involvement in Project Finance for Permanence (PFP), Blue Bonds, or sovereign debt restructuring initiatives.
